text:
The freight forwarders argue that they operate under additional handicaps. They are forced to rely on other modes of transportation for both linehaul transportation and assembly and distribution beyond terminal area limits. Specifically, this renders freight forwarders "captive clients" of certificated carriers resulting in exorbitant rates for assembly and distribution. The forwarders presented evidence that the costs attributable to the assembly and distribution component of the total transportation services they must purchase are rising at a disproportionate rate. The forwarders also complain that they are responsible to their customers for the service deficiencies of these other modes and yet have no control over them. We must point out, however, that this reliance on other transportation modes is largely dictated by statute. Furthermore, if there is a profit to be made in providing these services on forwarder traffic, there will be sufficient competition among carriers providing such services that the forwarders should be able to obtain adequate assembly and distribution service at a reasonable price. Finally, the forwarders can utilize section 409 contracts to procure favorable rates 50 from motor carriers for assembly and distribution services.
Section 409 of the Act allows freight forwarders and motor common carriers to enter into contracts setting special rates for forwarder utilization of motor carrier services. Section 409 rates can apply to assembly and distribution and linehaul movements of up to 450 miles. Section 408 of the Act permits motor common carriers to publish special rates for forwarder assembly and distribution services when those services can be provided at a lower cost than ordinary shorthaul small shipment services. It must be noted, however, that the preferred method of arranging assembly and distribution rates is under section 409. Section 409 rates can be customized to accomodate a specific forwarder, whereas section 408 rates are open to all forwarders and "others who employ or utilize the instrumentalities or services of such common carriers under like conditions..." 49 U.S.C. §$1008-1009 (1970).
